# CI: merge-queue and release jobs now run on self-hosted Linux and macOS runners

## What

CI has been rebalanced onto the organization's self-hosted runner pool (Linux X64 and macOS ARM64 machines):

- **Merge-queue legs** (`ci.yml` on `merge_group` events):
  - `quality`, `coverage-shard`, `coverage`, `integration`, `package-check` and `security` run on `[self-hosted, Linux, X64]`.
  - The per-OS matrix job `memory-recall-regression` sends its `ubuntu-latest` cells to `[self-hosted, Linux, X64]` and its `macos-latest` cells to `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
  - The `unit` and `smoke` matrices stay on GitHub-hosted runners for every OS. In the first routed queue run the self-hosted Linux hosts ran `unit` shards at 29-40+ minutes against this job's 40-minute ceiling (two of six shards were killed at the limit) and could not finish `smoke` inside its 15-minute window, while the self-hosted macs failed a broad class of subprocess-spawning suites (spawned children exited before the bounds under test could fire). Both stay GitHub-hosted until those are root-caused on the pool.
  - `php-validation`, the Windows `rust-sandbox-runner`, and the small gate jobs (`detect-release`, `release-owner-guard`, `detect-paths`, `unit-passed`) stay on GitHub-hosted runners.
- **Trusted-event jobs**: `stale.yml`, `quarantine-aging.yml`, and the scheduled/`workflow_dispatch` legs of `host-contract-check.yml` run on `[self-hosted, Linux, X64]`. `release-and-publish.yml` deliberately stays on `ubuntu-latest`: npm trusted publishing (OIDC provenance) does not support self-hosted runners, and those jobs carry publish credentials, so they keep their original runner until a supported publishing path is chosen explicitly.

Routing is expressed per job, so one job definition keeps every leg on the right runner. Every route names an explicit OS and architecture: every self-hosted runner carries the `self-hosted` label whatever its OS, so a bare `self-hosted` could land on the wrong machine. Matrix values are unchanged, so required-check names such as `unit (macos-latest, 3)` are unchanged.

Self-hosted machines persist between jobs and run several runner instances per host, so the seven routed `ci.yml` jobs each begin by pointing `TMPDIR` at their per-job `RUNNER_TEMP` (emptied by the runner for every job). Files left behind by an earlier job, such as a stray `.swarm` directory, cannot leak into the next one. Each of them also probes for a Bun matching the workflow's pinned version and skips setup-bun's release download only on an exact match, so a host with the pinned Bun pre-staged never touches the WAN for toolchain setup; a missing or mismatched Bun (and hosted legs, where the probe does not run) falls back to the pinned install instead of failing the job. Each job also points `BUN_CACHE` at its own `RUNNER_TEMP` directory: the live `~/.bun/install/cache` is shared by every runner instance on a host and concurrent installs corrupted it.

A small class of test suites — those asserting child-process exit/buffering semantics and wall-clock bounds (`bunSpawn` stream/output-coherence, `*-subprocess-bounds`, `external-tool-runner-node-fallback`, `store-replay-bounds`, and sandbox AC-008/AC-010) — skips under coverage shards only: coverage instrumentation distorts those semantics on shared self-hosted hosts, and the coverage gate fails on any single test. The hosted unit matrix keeps every one of them enforced.

The jobs in `stale.yml`, `quarantine-aging.yml` and `host-contract-check.yml` keep the runner's default temp root. None of them runs the repository test suite, which is what creates the `.swarm` scratch state the isolation above guards against; `publish-npm` is the largest of them at eleven steps, running a build and the package smoke check. If any of them later gains a test-suite step, it needs the isolation step too.

## Why

The org's 20-job GitHub-hosted pool has been the bottleneck: at peak, merge-group matrice

# TUI: no unconditional raw console output on the plugin init path (issue #3405)

## What

The three unconditional raw `console.warn` calls on the plugin init path in `src/index.ts` are gone or opt-in:

- The startup version banner (`[opencode-swarm] running vX.Y.Z`, issue #2236) now rides the debug-gated logger (visible under `OPENCODE_SWARM_DEBUG=1`, on stdout with the logger's `[opencode-swarm <timestamp>]` envelope). A raw stderr leg remains available behind the new opt-in `OPENCODE_SWARM_VERSION_BANNER=1` env var for headless/CLI stale-cache diagnosis; that leg keeps the historical line byte-for-byte, so log scrapers and the v2-dual-shape spike harness keep matching it.
- The project-root ownership redirect and fail-closed hints (issue #2679) no longer have a raw stderr leg. They were already double-buffered — the same text still reaches the operator via `/swarm diagnose` (`addDeferredWarning` + `advisoryWarn`) and the debug log, and the redirect record under `.swarm/advisories/` is unchanged.

## Why

In an in-process OpenCode TUI, plugin stderr renders as a full-width overlay pasted over the UI/input area, corrupting the session transcript (the #1249 class; the repo's `advisoryWarn` contract keeps TUI-owned paths off raw stderr/stdout). The version banner fired on every boot; the ownership hints fired on every redirected or fail-closed boot.

## Consumer coordination

- `spikes/v2-dual-shape/run-spike.mjs` now sets `OPENCODE_SWARM_VERSION_BANNER=1` in its host-spawn env so its banner-detection regexes keep proving plugin load (v2 does not relay plugin stdout, so the debug-logger leg is not a dependable spike signal).
- The #2679 ownership suites' hint assertion was retargeted from the raw console capture to the deferred-warning buffer (same child-path-masking hygiene; both call sites kept), with a new negative assertion that neither console stream carries the hint.
- New guardrails: `tests/unit/index-init-tui-quiet-3405.test.ts` (real plugin boots in redirect / fail-closed / banner / debug-hint modes) and statement-anchored source pins in `tests/unit/plugin-tui-safety.test.ts` (no raw hint warn statements; advisory legs retained; exactly one banner warn gated by the env var).

## Known caveats

- The two ownership hints are delivered through the in-memory deferred-warning buffer, which is cleared at the next plugin start. `/swarm diagnose` therefore shows them for the current session only. The redirect leg also writes the durable `.swarm/advisories/bootstrap-root-redirect.json` record; the fail-closed leg has no durable artifact.
- One always-raw init-path warning is intentionally retained: the `.swarm/`-files-are-Git-tracked hygiene warning (`src/utils/gitignore-warning.ts`), a must-see security exception the repo pins deliberately.
- Under the documented `quiet: false` mode the plugin still prints its verbose startup advisories to stderr, as before.

## Environment

- New env var `OPENCODE_SWARM_VERSION_BANNER=1` (default off) — documented in `docs/configuration.md`.

---

Correct six stale action version comments in ci.yml left behind by dependabot pin merges: the download-artifact v8.0.2 commit was labeled v4.3.0 on two lines and the upload-artifact v7.0.2 commit was labeled v7.0.1 on four lines. Version comments are the interface dependabot uses for version detection, so mislabeled pins can generate bogus future bump PRs. No pin values change; the required-check-contract ci.yml hash is refreshed accordingly.

---

# Guardrails: allow file authority within linked git worktrees

## Summary

- When executing agent sessions inside a Git worktree or inspecting files across worktrees of the same repository, file authority checks could incorrectly fail with `AUTHORITY_ROOT_ESCAPE` (`target resolves outside the working directory`).
- Root cause: `checkFileAuthorityWithRules` assumed all valid file paths must be strictly contained within `dir` (`cwd`). In multi-worktree workflows, worktrees of the same repository live in sibling directories outside `dir`.
- Fix: `checkFileAuthorityWithRules` now discovers linked worktrees via `git worktree list --porcelain` (cached in LRU with a 60 s TTL) and treats files located within any valid linked worktree of the repository as workspace-contained.

## Changes

- Adds bounded discovery: `getLinkedGitWorktrees(dir)` with LRU cache (60 s expiry, so worktrees created or removed mid-session — and transient git failures — are re-queried), a 1500 ms timeout, explicit byte bound, `windowsHide`, and `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR` stripped from the subprocess environment.
- Worktree roots are validated before they can widen containment: `bare` records are skipped, and every linked root must back-anchor to this repository — its `.git` file must reference a registration under this repository's `.git/worktrees/` whose own `gitdir` entry names the root back. This rejects registrations whose target has no cooperating `.git` pointer and registrations naming other repositories. Scope: worktree trust remains git-native trust — a target directory holding a `.git` pointer left by earlier git history (moved, copied, or pruned worktree folders) still validates, because git itself cannot distinguish that from a real `git worktree add`; sessions inside a bare clone's linked worktree get no trusted roots (fail-closed, same as before this change).
- Re-roots to the LONGEST (most specific) matching worktree root, so deny rules resolve against the right root in nested layouts.
- On Windows, worktree roots and targets are canonicalized through the native realpath (expanding 8.3 short-name forms such as `RUNNER~1` and stripping the `\\?\` device prefix) before containment comparison; write targets that do not exist yet are canonicalized via their nearest existing ancestor so not-yet-created files inside a linked worktree still match.
- A re-rooted target whose ancestor chain crosses a symlink/junction inside the matched worktree is denied (`AUTHORITY_ROOT_ESCAPE`), closing the new-file-write redirect path.
- Declared scope for coders is evaluated once, in the re-rooted coordinate system (the raw-path second evaluation is removed).
- Unit coverage in `tests/unit/hooks/guardrails-worktree-authority.test.ts` (sibling-layout allow/deny paths) and `tests/unit/hooks/guardrails-worktree-containment-hardening.test.ts` (cooperating and non-cooperating forged registrations, bare repositories, longest-match re-rooting, planted symlinks). Repository content that a trusted worktree's own scripts invoke (hook scripts, build steps) remains subject to the repository's own policies, as at base.

## Known caveats

- The worktree-root cache expires after 60 s; within that window a worktree added or removed mid-session is not reflected.
- Discovery runs a bounded synchronous `git worktree list` on the guard path for targets that escape `cwd` containment (at most once per directory per 60 s).

---

# Delegation gate: configurable acceptance criteria auto-injection

## Summary

- Adds the opt-in `hooks.auto_inject_acceptance` setting (default: `false`).
- When enabled, a `coder` or `reviewer` delegation that has no `ACCEPTANCE:` line, or only an empty one, is no longer rejected with `ACCEPTANCE_FIELD_REQUIRED`. The gate writes a generic default requirement into the dispatch, marked `(auto-injected default: ...)`, and queues an `ACCEPTANCE AUTO-INJECTED` advisory for the dispatching session (when that session is registered).
- With the default (`false`), the existing strict fail-closed behavior is unchanged.

## Changes

- Adds `auto_inject_acceptance` to `HooksConfigSchema` in `src/config/schema.ts` and `opencode-swarm.schema.json`.
- `createDelegationGateHook` in `src/hooks/delegation-gate.ts` fills an empty `ACCEPTANCE:` header in the field that actually carries it (line endings preserved), or appends a block to `prompt` (else the first text field). It never fabricates a field: if the dispatch has no text field at all, the strict rejection stands. The signal is emitted only after the injected text passes the same validator.
- `config doctor` now derives its known-hook allowlist from `HooksConfigSchema`, so the new key (and the previously missing `background_subagents` and `background_pending_timeout_minutes`) is no longer reported as an unknown hook field that `--fix` would remove.
- Documents the setting in `docs/configuration.md`.
- Adds tests: `tests/unit/hooks/delegation-gate-acceptance-autoinject.test.ts` (injection, preservation, flag-off, field targeting, CRLF/NBSP, advisory) and `tests/unit/services/config-doctor-hooks-parity.test.ts`.

## Known caveats

- The injected requirement is generic, not task-derived. For a single task mapped to spec requirements the verbatim `FR-###`/`SC-###` text is still appended and coverage-checked, but an unmapped task or a multi-task phase/council reviewer dispatch only receives the generic line.
- Project config can set this key (as it can `hooks.delegation_gate`); it has no user-level-only protection.
- The motivating OpenCode v2 behavior (a hook-thrown rejection not being rendered to the model) is not verifiable in this repository.

---

# Guardrails: `authority.enabled: false` no longer rejects custom or host agents as unknown

## Summary

- With `authority.enabled: false`, writes by agents that the plugin has no authority classification for (for example custom host agents such as `sre-planner`, `builder` or `infra`) were rejected with `AUTHORITY_UNKNOWN_AGENT` ("Unknown agent: no authority classification exists"), even though authority enforcement had been switched off.
- Root cause: in `checkFileAuthorityWithRules` the unknown-agent denial ran for every agent regardless of `authority.enabled`, and `buildEffectiveRules` returns only the built-in role rules while authority is disabled.
- Fix: while authority is disabled, an agent without a classification is no longer denied merely for being unknown. It still passes through the hard-policy checks first and is then allowed.

## Behavior change

- This applies only when you set `authority.enabled: false`. The default (`true`) is unchanged: unclassified agents are still denied with `AUTHORITY_UNKNOWN_AGENT`.
- While authority is disabled, these checks still apply to every agent that reaches them: path safety and workspace containment, the configured `authority.universal_deny_prefixes` (empty by default), the canonical read-only and dedicated-tool-only roles, the coder `.git`/`.swarm` protection, and verifier-config protection for the built-in swarm roles.
- Newly admitted (unclassified) agents are additionally denied writes to `.git/` and `.swarm/` with `AUTHORITY_PROTECTED_PATH` when they use the file-write tools (write, edit, patch). Shell-command writes keep following the existing shell-path rules, which are unchanged. They remain able to write other workspace paths, including verifier and C
